transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-03 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Evan Morales (Tidal Head of ML), Priya Desai (Platform), Samir Khan (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): quick demo of picklist flows, showed how to filter for quantized variants and how bench signals map to expected latency/cost; customer asked about private VPC and audit logs.

[00:00] Jordan Park: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um we appreciate you carving out time. this is jordan from redwood, i'm the ae on the account, with maya our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Evan Morales: good, thanks jordan. excited to see the picklist flow — we're trying to compress model selection time, we have a couple of internal constraints to share.
[00:20] Priya Desai: hi all, jump in later, we're especially interested in how we keep p95 under 120ms for short prompts.
[00:26] Maya Singh: perfect, we'll focus on the picklist UX, filters for hardware and quantization, then walk through bench signals and compatibility matrix mapping to kernels.

[02:10] Jordan Park: quick agenda — 1) catalog filter and picklist demo, 2) bench signal interpretation, 3) compatibility matrix and what it means for runtime, 4) Q&A and next steps. sound right?
[02:22] Samir Khan: yep, good. also can we cover audit logs and VPC briefly?
[02:29] Maya Singh: sure, we will touch on it at the end.

[04:05] Maya Singh: alright i'm sharing screen — this is the redwood console, model catalog area. first thing is the picklist, which we try to keep minimal for an engineer: you search by task (chat/generation/embedding), then filter by latency profile, memory footprint, and quantization tier.
[04:32] Evan Morales: i see tags for "fp16", "int8", "mixed" — the int8 results look interesting, do you have perf numbers attached?
[04:39] Maya Singh: yes, each model line shows our verified perf profile — median token latency, p95 by sequence length, and a cost index. note these are from our hosted fleet but we also include dedicated-simulated numbers. sometimes transcription here says "simulated" as "simu-led" which is goofy.

[06:05] Priya Desai: can we filter to only models that have private-deploy supported? we have strict data residency needs.
[06:12] Maya Singh: yep toggle the "private deploy" filter — that trims to models we vet for KMS/HSM integrations and E2E encryption. you'll notice a compatibility matrix link to the right, click that.
[06:30] Jordan Park: real quick — on private deploys there's two modes: vpc-managed (redwood control plane in your VPC) and fully on-prem package. both ship with audit logs, role-based access, and we can bring your KMS.

[08:00] Maya Singh: compatibility matrix opens — rows are model families, columns are runtime kernels and hardware backends. green means native kernel exists for that quant profile; yellow means we do a fallback kernel with some perf tradeoffs.
[08:18] Evan Morales: whoa okay so for that 7B model i see green on A100-amx but yellow on t4-int8, is that because kernel support is missing?
[08:28] Maya Singh: right, we map operator coverage and attention optimizations. sometimes smaller cards need different kernel paths so you may see a higher p95. we surface the estimated p95 delta in ms when you hover.

[10:15] Priya Desai: how accurate are those deltas? our infra team gets nervous when numbers are optimistic.
[10:21] Maya Singh: they're empirically derived from our bench fleet across representative sequences — we add a safety margin; transcription might read as "safety margin" as "safety manage" occasionally. for enterprise pilots we recommend a short bench sprint to validate on your exact prompts and payload shapes.

[12:40] Jordan Park: quick interjection — we also show bench signals like tokenization overhead, kv-cache hit rates, and memory blowup probability. Evan, you mentioned short prompts, we can show the p50/p95 for sequences of length 16 and 64.
[12:58] Evan Morales: yes please, sequence 16 is our primary SLO.

[14:05] Maya Singh: switching bench view — here's a side-by-side of three candidate models: open-7B-int8, open-13B-mix, and open-7B-fp16. notice the cost index, and the latency curves. open-7B-int8 has lower token cost but p95 is 140ms on t4 in our sim, while on tpu or a100 it's ~85ms.
[14:36] Evan Morales: hmm 140ms on t4 is above our 120ms p95 target, but on a100 it's great — our infra team runs cheaper cards though.
[14:45] Maya Singh: that's a common tradeoff — routing can help. you can set a policy: default to int8 on cheaper hardware but if p95 exceeds 120ms for a given request class, route to a higher-tier variant pinned to a100/dedicated pool. the redwood runtime supports automatic fallback.

[17:00] Priya Desai: for the fallback, is it seamless? do tokens get re-generated or do we pay double?
[17:09] Maya Singh: good question. fallbacks are request-level — if the request hits the cheaper variant and the runtime detects it will exceed SLO, it reroutes before generation starts. so you don't double-bill; we try to avoid partial generations. there are modes where you can allow partial recovery, but default is pre-flight routing.

[19:10] Samir Khan: what's the overhead for pre-flight checks? we can't add noticeable latency to each request.
[19:17] Maya Singh: pre-flight checks are lightweight heuristics based on sequence length, cached prefix matches, and a small ML classifier. typical added latency is sub-2ms, we show this in the console under "routing overhead".

[21:30] Jordan Park: pivoting — let's talk about how to use the picklist to narrow candidates quickly. two tips: 1) start with throughput and SLO columns, 2) add a bench signal column for your prompt set. the picklist remembers recent runs.
[21:50] Evan Morales: can we import our bench results into the console? we have internal benchmarks already.
[21:57] Maya Singh: yes CSV import — map columns to sequence length, latency, tokens/sec, and the console will annotate model lines with your real-world numbers. that's actually how the compatibility matrix can show your delta vs our fleet.

[24:05] Priya Desai: on the security side, quick question — does private deploy include our SSO and audit streams?
[24:13] Jordan Park: yes, we support SAML SSO integration, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via syslog or S3 for long-term retention. for regulated industries we also offer HSM-backed KMS.

[26:30] Maya Singh: back to bench signals — we flagged three models where kv-cache blowup risk is high for long contexts. for your use case (mostly short contexts) it's low, so we can de-prioritize those. transcription note: sometimes the system tags get garbled — e.g., "kv cache" becomes "kay vee cache" in the transcript.

[28:40] Evan Morales: interesting, also curious about quantization artifacts — do you provide quality regression numbers? we can't sacrifice answer fidelity for a small cost win.
[28:50] Maya Singh: yes we have a quality monitoring widget — it shows evals on your prompt set (if provided) or on our curated evals: perplexity deltas, rouge/bleu-ish metrics where applicable, and human-review flags. we recommend a baseline A/B between fp16 and int8 on a small holdout.

[30:55] Jordan Park: i want to highlight the "compatibility score" column — it's a single heuristic combining kernel coverage, bench stability, and fallback friction. it's not perfect but useful to triage.
[31:12] Priya Desai: can we tune the weighting? for us kernel coverage matters more than cost.
[31:18] Maya Singh: absolutely — the picklist has a "weight config" modal, you can bump kernel coverage to 70% weight and cost to 10% for your team's view. these views can be saved and shared with teammates.

[33:40] Evan Morales: what's the best starting shortlist you'd recommend for our SLO (p95 120ms, short prompts, wanting to avoid extra infra spend)?
[33:49] Maya Singh: i'd start with open-7B-int8 for cost, open-7B-fp16 for latency, and a 13B mixed if you want higher quality. then run a 2-4 hour bench sprint to validate p95 on your exact workload. if int8 fails p95 consistently, use routing to promote to fp16 in peak windows.

[36:00] Jordan Park: i'm going to demo the bench-sprint template — it's a git-like YAML that defines prompt set, concurrency, target p95, and the hardware matrix to test.
[36:18] Maya Singh: here's the sample output from a sprint — heatmap of p95 vs cost, plus kernel warnings. you can export the full matrix as CSV or push to your internal perf tracker via our API.

[38:55] Priya Desai: can the bench run inside our VPC? we'd prefer not to send sample prompts out.
[39:02] Maya Singh: yes, for private deployments the bench runner can run in your network — we provide an agent that streams anonymized metrics only. no request payloads leave your VPC unless you opt-in.

[41:10] Evan Morales: good. a couple of procurement/security asks: SOC2 type 2 report, iso, and an option for data residency in eu-west.
[41:20] Jordan Park: we've got SOC2 and ISO certs; we'll attach the compliance pack. eu-west deployment is supported — for private we can deploy control plane in that region or push on-prem.

[43:45] Samir Khan: are there any known gotchas with our existing infra? we run mostly g4dn-type equivalent nodes for cost reasons.
[43:53] Maya Singh: g4-like cards will show good throughput for smaller models but int8 coverage can be limited — that's where the compatibility matrix flags yellow. fallback policies are your friend here.

[46:00] Priya Desai: i'd like to see an export of the compatibility matrix filtered to our hardware types and the 10 models you recommended.
[46:07] Jordan Park: we'll generate that and include it in the deliverables.

[47:20] Evan Morales: ok high level recap — 1) we'll run a bench sprint with redwood in our VPC or using the agent, 2) redwood sends catalog export and filtered compatibility matrix, 3) we'll share prompt set and SLOs.
[47:35] Maya Singh: yes and se will be hands-on for the bench sprint.

[48:10] Jordan Park: anything else on security or procurement?
[48:15] Samir Khan: procurement wants cost estimates for both hosted and dedicated options for our monthly token volumes.
[48:22] Jordan Park: noted — i'll include a cost comparison table with committed vs on-demand assumptions.

[49:52] Priya Desai: last quick Q: do you track model drift in the console?
[49:58] Maya Singh: we do — quality monitors and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. you can configure thresholds and auto-rollbacks to previous pinned versions. transcription sometimes misses "rollbacks" as "roll backs" but context is fine.

[51:10] Jordan Park: great, thanks everyone for the time. we'll send the matrix and pricing by monday, set up the bench sprint candidate week of 6/14.
[51:22] Evan Morales: thanks, appreciate it.
[51:26] Samir Khan: thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript.
